_execution_note: CPU with many workers. The backend crossover measured CuPy at 7.41 labels/s against NumPy's 2.62 at 12 qubits but capped at one parent worker, so eight CPU workers win by about 3x.
_scope_note: The learned comparison on REAL Pegasus connectivity, 10-14 physical qubits. The main experiment runs on synthetic quotient graphs at 3-10 qubits; this asks the same questions -- does bank selection beat a fixed schedule, and does an embedding-aware encoder beat a blind one -- where the coupling graph is the vendor's. 96 parents split 72/12/24 by parent, 864 train records. Three seeds rather than five because each record is 10-14 qubits instead of 3-10. No spectral teacher is possible above 10 qubits, so the privileged-oracle comparison does NOT extend here and must not be quoted from this run.
